The user wants Japanese UI microcopy for an EC app:
- s1: empty cart screen message (there's already a "商品を探す" button at the bottom)
- s2: dialog title for confirming deletion of an item in the cart
- s3: button to execute deletion
- s4: button to cancel

The skill is in Chinese (Taiwan) but the output must be Japanese for a Japanese EC app. The language conventions (zh-tw lexicon) don't directly apply to Japanese, but the principles do: roles fix form, no affect, no unnecessary clauses, conventional labels.

Let me think about Japanese conventions:

s1: empty state. Form: noun or state; the action lives on the button (already present as 「商品を探す」). So the empty state message should be just the state: 「カートは空です」or「カートに商品がありません」. No coaching like「下のボタンから商品を探しましょう」 since the button already exists. Common Japanese EC conventions: 「カートに商品がありません」 is very standard (楽天, Amazon: 「カートに商品はありません」). Actually Amazon Japan: 「カートは空です」. Rakuten: 「カートに商品がありません」. Both fine. The empty role says: noun or state; the action lives on the button. So 「カートに商品がありません」 is standard.

Note: no period for such short strings; Japanese typical: カートに商品がありません。 Actually status sentences may have 。 but Japanese UI usually doesn't use 。 in short labels. Standard: カートに商品がありません (no period).

s2: dialog title. Role: names the act, noun or verb phrase, no question mark. Japanese: 「商品を削除」or「商品の削除」. Common Japanese dialog titles: 「削除の確認」 or 「商品を削除しますか？」 — but no question mark per doctrine for dialog titles? The doctrine says dialog-title: names the act, noun or verb phrase, no question mark. Japanese convention often uses questions in confirmation dialogs, but the skill says dialog title names the act. So 「商品を削除」 or 「商品の削除」. Hmm, Japanese iOS conventions: alerts often like 「「〇〇」を削除しますか？」 with title. But the skill's role contract says dialog-title should name the act without question mark. Let me follow the skill: 「商品の削除」 or 「商品を削除」. Verb phrase 「商品を削除」 reads like a button label too. Noun phrase 「商品の削除」 is clearly a title. I'll go with 「商品の削除」.

Actually wait — the deletion is of a cart item. Could be 「カートから削除」. The act: removing the item from the cart. 「カートから削除」 names the act precisely. Hmm, but the dialog appears when deleting an item from cart. 「商品の削除」 might imply deleting the product itself (from account?). In cart context, 「カートから削除」 is clearer and unambiguous. I think 「カートから削除」 or 「商品をカートから削除」. Let me think about dialog body — not requested. Title: 「カートから削除」 — names the act, no question. Good.

s3: button to execute deletion: 「削除」. Imperative verb phrase, conventional. Japanese confirms: 削除する? Conventional is 「削除」. Apple/Material Japanese: 「削除」. Good.

s4: cancel button: 「キャンセル」. The doctrine: keep conventional action labels; cancel stays Cancel. In Japanese, キャンセル is the conventional label. Good.

Should s1 mention that the state exists: 「カートに商品がありません」. Also fine: 「カートは空です」. Which is more conventional in Japanese EC? Rakuten Ichiba cart empty: 「現在、カートに商品がありません。」 Amazon: カートは空です。 Yahoo!ショッピング: 「カートに商品がありません」. I'll use 「カートに商品がありません」.

No extra clauses like 「下の『商品を探す』ボタンからお好きな商品をお探しください」 — the button already exists; deletion test removes it.

Output JSON only: {"s1":"カートに商品がありません","s2":"カートから削除","s3":"削除","s4":"キャンセル"}

The user asked for JSON only. So respond with just the JSON. No extra text, no code fences? "JSONのみを返してください" — return only JSON. I'll return the raw JSON without markdown fences. Probably safest to output exactly the JSON object.</think>{"s1":"カートに商品がありません","s2":"カートから削除","s3":"削除","s4":"キャンセル"}
